goal: As medical secretary for Heartland Orthopedic Specialists, audit February 2026 referrals against the ICD-10 M00-M99 codes (chapter, narrative and laterality), flag data-quality issues and duplicates, and build a 3-tab audit workbook with conditional formatting. Also produce a dual-purpose records/clarification fax template (HIPAA 45 CFR 164.508), a referral acknowledgment template, and a three-tier action plan.
delivered: February_2026_Referral_Audit.xlsx (Referral Log with audit columns plus red/yellow fills and conditional-formatting rules, Discrepancy Report, Summary Dashboard), Records_and_Clarification_Request.docx, Referral_Acknowledgment_Letter.docx and February_2026_Action_Plan.docx. It caught the S-code, both femur and Achilles laterality errors with corrected codes, the Thompson duplicate, and an extra M25.561 right/left knee mismatch on REF-0211.
what_went_wrong: The agent never noticed insurance ID AET-5567201 shared by Thompson and unrelated patient Brenda Washington. Several items failed on missing explanations: no 'wrong-site procedure' risk note for the Patel laterality error, no malignancy rationale for urgent scheduling, no consolidation recommendation for the duplicate, and no attached-HIPAA-form reference or confidentiality notice in the fax template. Two items look like grading problems: the Referral Log has correct red/yellow fills and CF rules the text-only judge could not see, and Angela Brooks was put in Tier 2, which the prompt's own definition (routine with authorization gap) supports.

failed_items.why: The REF-0210 mismatch, the correct M84.452A code and the Dr. Patel/fax contact all passed. The item failed only because no file explains that laterality errors risk wrong-site procedures; the Discrepancy Report just says 'Laterality mismatch / urgent clinical clarification'.

The staged CSV shows AET-5567201 on REF-0202, REF-0218 (Thompson) and REF-0217 (Washington, a different patient). The agent imported these rows but never checked for ID collisions; the Discrepancy Report issue types cover no insurance-ID anomaly.

REF-0210 is correctly in Tier 1 with oncology coordination and the Patel contact, but the action text ('Coordinate oncology referral noted; no appointment scheduled') never ties urgency to the suspected malignancy in the CSV's Referral_Reason.

A subagent retrieved the pacortho.org release form (step 485), yet the template only has a 45 CFR 164.508(c) checklist 'not itself a patient authorization'. It names no attached HIPAA Authorization Release Form and has no fax confidentiality notice; letterhead, merge fields and the 10-day deadline passed.

Referral Log does have formatting: CF rule A2:AC19 '$Q2="Urgent"' (fill F4CCCC) and R2:S19 '="No"' (fill FFF2CC), plus static fills on exactly the 6 urgent rows and the No cells, including both on 0212/0217 (checked with openpyxl). The judge saw only a text dump and said no fill exists.

The prompt defines Tier 2 as 'routine referrals with outstanding documentation or authorization gaps'. REF-0211 is Routine with Auth_Status 'Not Submitted' and a real M25.561 (right) vs 'left knee' laterality error the agent caught, so Tier 2 follows the stated definitions. The rubric's Tier 3 placement contradicts them.

All entries carry contact, practice and fax, but the duplicate REF-0202/0218 actions say 'confirm second-opinion workflow' rather than recommending consolidation with the paired REF-ID. The CSV note does say the patient seeks a second opinion, so this is a judgment miss.

subagent_notes: Two subagents: one inspected the CRMC referral form PDF for letterhead (read_image error, but it reported layout), and one researched the k4m1113 ICD-10 codes.csv and pacortho release form (one ecfr.gov fetch error, but it found the sources). Both gave usable findings; neither caused the failures, which came from root's analysis and drafting.
